extracted.intended_audience: OSTP, OMB, White House policymakers, federal agencies, and federal regulators
extracted.subtask_description: Civil-rights coalition comments recommending standards and concrete policy actions to ensure a National AI Strategy is centered on equity, civil rights, and trustworthy AI across federal agencies, procurement, enforcement, workforce, and public services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Center National AI Strategy on equity and civil rights
rubrics_metrics.description: The National AI Strategy must be centered on equity and civil rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy actions should prioritize mitigating discriminatory automated systems that cause concrete harms (loss of economic opportunities, denial of loans, adverse employment outcomes, lower-quality health care, barriers to housing). Centering equity is a precondition for achieving other goals like national security or global competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make the AI Bill of Rights binding via OMB guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Make the AI Bill of Rights binding administration policy through OMB guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OMB, DPC, and OSTP should require that steps in the AI Bill of Rights are taken for all automated systems the U.S. government develops, deploys, uses, acquires, or funds; guidance should be responsive to relevant statutes (AI in Government Act, Advancing American AI Act), update prior OMB guidance, be required of all agencies, and be developed with public input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinated interagency follow-through under EO 14091 and AI Bill of Rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure coordinated follow-through by federal agencies in light of Executive Order 14091 and the AI Bill of Rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete actions from the Oct 2022 fact sheet without delay (e.g., HUD guidance on tenant screening). Agencies (EEOC, OSHA, DOJ, Labor) should issue/enforce guidance on hiring tech, algorithmic worker management, workplace surveillance. DOJ should ensure procurement and use of law enforcement technologies advance equitable justice. White House should staff National AI Initiative Office and ensure Interagency Policy Committee on AI and Equity functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustained public engagement with diverse stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: Launch sustained public engagement with diverse stakeholders to raise awareness of AI harms and support mitigation efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administration should convene diverse experts, model participatory processes centering impacted communities, amplify examples of AI-driven harms, and ensure sector-specific NIST profiles include robust civil society participation and White House oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shift from principles to durable, measurable, enforceable safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: Shift focus from high-level principles to durable, measurable, enforceable, and robust safeguards for AI use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Move beyond statements of principle to concrete policy measures, enforcement mechanisms, and measurable obligations for developers, deployers, and agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whole-of-society plan to implement the Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Build a whole-of-society plan for implementing the Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights as part of the National AI Strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan should address how federal regulators and private sector actors can apply the AI Bill of Rights to new and existing technologies and outline concrete steps for implementation across stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize disproportionate impacts on historically marginalized groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider and prioritize the disproportionate impact algorithmic discrimination has on communities of color and historically marginalized groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that people facing discrimination (race, ethnicity, national origin, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, income, immigration status, disability) are more likely to be harmed and often lack resources to respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure AI systems are usable and accessible for people with disabilities and language differences
rubrics_metrics.description: AI systems must be usable by all members of the community, including people with disabilities and speakers of different languages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Developers should intentionally include disabled people, build systems that conform to accessibility standards, and consider language impacts to ensure accessibility where systems are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre- and post-deployment impact assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: Require deployment of impact assessments before and after AI system deployment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impact assessments should be part of concrete steps in the National AI Strategy to identify harms, monitor systems over time, and inform mitigation and remediation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disparity testing and mitigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Deploy disparity testing and mitigation measures to detect and address unequal outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include requirements for disparity testing in development and ongoing monitoring, and mandate mitigation when disparities are found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data minimization and robust privacy protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement data minimization requirements and privacy protections for AI systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit collection and retention of data, prohibit predatory commercial surveillance practices that fuel data-driven discrimination, and integrate privacy safeguards into system design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and explainability requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Require transparency about when and how AI is used and ensure explainability of automated decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because many systems are 'black box', impacted communities must be informed and have recourse; transparency obligations should include public-facing disclosure and avenues for contesting errors/rights violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide human alternatives to automated systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure availability of human alternatives to automated decision systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: People must have pathways to human review or human-in-the-loop options where automated systems affect rights, benefits, or opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equip federal agencies to enforce consumer protection and civil rights laws in AI context
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the federal government is prepared to enforce laws related to AI, including evaluating needs for technical talent and resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National AI Strategy should address staffing, technical expertise, and resource needs of enforcement agencies to handle AI-related cases and oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish or resource Offices of Civil Rights in agencies with technical experts
rubrics_metrics.description: Expand or create within each agency an Office of Civil Rights resourced with technical experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These offices should be empowered and funded to address civil rights issues arising from agency use of AI systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on mitigating job losses and promoting good jobs
rubrics_metrics.description: Include strategy components to mitigate job displacement and harness AI for creation of good jobs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National AI Strategy should support labor protections, worker privacy, reskilling, ensuring new jobs are quality jobs with collective bargaining rights, and promote minority participation in new roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhance labor protections and ban discriminatory or privacy-violating AI uses in the workplace
rubrics_metrics.description: Enhance labor protections and ban certain AI uses or practices that are potentially discriminatory or violate worker privacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should consider prohibitions on problematic surveillance and management tools; ensure enforcement and guidance from EEOC, OSHA, DOJ, and Labor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase transparency about business practices and data usage affecting workers and consumers
rubrics_metrics.description: Require greater transparency about data and business practices of AI deployers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency should cover how systems use data, how they affect workers/consumers, and corporate practices that contribute to harms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure collective bargaining addresses AI impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure collective bargaining mechanisms include AI-related workplace issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage or require that labor agreements can address deployment, monitoring, and impacts of AI on work conditions and job quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use tax policy to direct AI development toward labor-augmenting outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider tax policy tools (taxes or tax credits) to incentivize development and adoption of labor-augmenting AI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tax incentives can be used to shape private sector choices and reward AI that augments rather than displaces workers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modernize Unemployment Insurance and consider job guarantees for widespread AI job losses
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure social safety nets are adequate for AI-driven job displacement, including modernizing UI and exploring job guarantees if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learn from models like Trade Adjustment Assistance and temporary UI expansions to design durable supports for displaced workers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reskilling and retraining must produce quality jobs and expand minority participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Reskilling and retraining programs should lead to quality jobs with collective bargaining rights and expand workforce participation for minority and historically disadvantaged communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure new roles created by AI include protections and opportunities for historically underrepresented groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participatory development for AI in public services and benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Involve impacted communities in developing and assessing AI systems used to deliver public services, including benefits determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Increased community involvement should occur throughout development and assessment to surface harms and preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for due process, transparency, and equal protection in benefits systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure due process, transparency, and equal protection through regulation and legislation for AI used in benefits determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal protections should be codified to protect rights of applicants and beneficiaries affected by automated decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish minimum standards for AI use in benefits determinations across lifecycle
rubrics_metrics.description: Set minimum standards for the use of AI in benefits determinations beginning prior to development and continuing after deployment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards should include design, testing, deployment, monitoring, and remediation requirements to prevent discriminatory outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit or strictly limit emotion recognition technology and inferences about emotional states
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat AI systems that claim to draw inferences about emotional states (ERT) as an unacceptable intrusion and restrict their use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ERT poses risks to privacy, freedom of thought, and can amplify discrimination (e.g., in hiring, education, policing); deployment can lead to severe real-world harms such as preemptive arrests regardless of inference reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require safeguards against algorithmic discrimination and black-box harms
rubrics_metrics.description: Mandate safeguards including data minimization, impact assessments, protections against algorithmic discrimination, and remedies for black-box system opacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because black-box systems deny transparency and recourse, the strategy should require mechanisms that enable contestation and accountability when rights violations occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oversight and civil society participation in NIST AI Risk Management Framework profiles
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure efforts to develop sector-specific 'profiles' for the NIST AI Risk Management Framework have strong oversight and robust civil society participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: White House participation and quality control are needed to ensure profiles adequately reflect civil rights concerns and include impacted communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include U.S. civil society input in international AI policy forums and agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure AI-related international agreements and councils include and reflect input from U.S. civil society stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forums such as the U.S.-EU Trade & Technology Council, Indo-Pacific Economic Framework, and Council of Europe Committee on AI should include civil society perspectives while advancing EO 14091 ideals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define 'trustworthy AI' as safe, effective, and equitable
rubrics_metrics.description: AI systems must be trustworthy — safe, effective, and equitable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other policy goals (national security, competitiveness) are unattainable without trustworthy AI; trustworthiness should be an explicit objective of the strategy with concrete enforcement steps.
